destination.tagline: Pinot noir country over the Remutaka Range from Wellington, running down to Cape Palliser.
destination.description: The Wairarapa is the south-eastern corner of the North Island, separated from the Wellington area by the Remutaka Range and popular with Wellington day-trippers. The Remutaka and Tararua ranges shelter it from the prevailing westerlies, giving a warm, dry climate, and wine centres on Martinborough, where pinot noir and sauvignon blanc are the two main varieties. Masterton is the largest town, with Carterton, Greytown and Featherston strung along the way. More than 1,000 people commute 'through the hill' to Wellington each day.
whyVisit: Taste pinot noir among Martinborough's vineyards
Walk to the Putangirua Pinnacles, filmed as the Paths of the Dead
Climb to Cape Palliser's lighthouse at the North Island's southern tip

goodToKnow.title: Trains stop at Masterton
goodToKnow.detail: The Wairarapa Line runs 91 km from Wellington to Masterton, with five services each way Monday to Thursday, six on Fridays, and only two at weekends and on public holidays. There is no train to Martinborough; Metlink bus 200 runs there from Masterton and Featherston, but not on Sundays or public holidays.

goodToKnow.title: Hire a bike, not a car
goodToKnow.detail: Martinborough's vineyards lie in ribbons around the north and east of town, and the Martinborough Wine Centre hires cycles (bookings essential), which avoids drinking and driving.

goodToKnow.title: Give seals 20 metres
goodToKnow.detail: DOC advises staying at least 20 metres from fur seals, which have sharp teeth and move quickly if threatened. Keep dogs leashed and away, and never get between a seal and the sea.

wairarapa-1.bio: A town laid out in 1879 in the pattern of the Union Jack, with vineyards in ribbons around its northern and eastern sides, best known for pinot noir.

wairarapa-2.bio: Eroded gravel pillars cut by the Pūtangirua Stream, seen best from the Pinnacles Ridge Track lookout and filmed as the Paths of the Dead in The Lord of the Rings.

wairarapa-3.bio: A red-and-white striped lighthouse from 1897 at the southern tip of the North Island, reached by 258 steps up a 58 m cliff.

wairarapa-4.bio: A limestone reef, lagoon and lighthouse beneath 162 m Castle Rock, the only place in the world where the shrubby Castlepoint daisy grows.

wairarapa-5.bio: A small town on State Highway 2 where New Zealand's first Arbor Day was celebrated in 1890, and which still keeps a register of its trees.

wairarapa-6.bio: An open-sky astronomical stone circle near Carterton, built by the Phoenix Astronomical Society on a similar scale to England's Stonehenge and laid out for the southern hemisphere sky.
wairarapa-6.hours: Self-guided 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily; guided tours 10:30, 12:30 and 2:00

wairarapa-7.bio: A road end 17 km from Masterton with a bookable DOC lodge, a campsite, Donnelly Flat picnic area and day walks, including the Atiwhakatu Track, plus the start of the 24 km Jumbo circuit.

wairarapa-8.bio: A Featherston museum holding H199 Mont Cenis, the only surviving Fell locomotive in the world, alongside a restored brakevan, photos and video.
wairarapa-8.hours: Saturday and Sunday 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM; closed public holidays

wairarapa-10.bio: A 942-hectare unfenced forest sanctuary on State Highway 2 where kiwi, kākā and takahē are bred and released, with a nocturnal kiwi house and daily feeding talks.

wairarapa-11.bio: A heritage village in Greytown built around the Hastwell stables and their cobblestone courtyard, with a colonial cottage, the Wairarapa's first public hospital, a country school and the Donald Woolshed.
wairarapa-11.hours: Sep–May 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM; Jun–Aug 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM (closed Christmas Day, New Year's Day, Good Friday and ANZAC Day morning)

wairarapa-12.bio: The Wairarapa's museum of art and history on Bruce Street in Masterton, with changing exhibitions from textile craft to inventions.

rimutaka-incline.bio: The old railway grade over the Remutaka Range, now part of an 18 km walking and cycling trail from Kaitoke to Cross Creek with restored bridges, tunnels (bring a torch) and a viewing platform.

kaitoke-regional-park.bio: A Greater Wellington park on the Hutt River with short bush walks, river swimming, the Kaitoke Weir and the Rivendell film location, entered from Waterworks Road.
kaitoke-regional-park.hours: 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM (1 April – 30 September); 6:00 AM – 9:00 PM (1 October – 31 March)

tararua-forest-park.bio: New Zealand's first forest park, established in 1954, 1,150 square kilometres of Tararua Range bush, huts and tracks, entered from Holdsworth, Waiohine Gorge or Ōtaki Forks.

remutaka-forest-park.bio: A 22,000-hectare forest park across the Remutaka Range, with a campground and swimming spots in the Catchpool Valley 30 km from Wellington and kiwi released since 2006.

tararua-southern-crossing.bio: An alpine tramp of about 32 km and two to three days from Ōtaki Forks over Mount Hector to Kaitoke, one of the Tararua Range's four classic tramps and graded advanced by DOC.
